name: Gran Paradiso National Park
blurb: Ibex saved from extinction, whistling marmots and eagles above the Alpine treeline.

tip.title: Take away the snow
tip.text: Snowmelt waters the short alpine growing season. Set Snow cover to -100% and watch the grasses and sedges, then the ibex, marmots and the wolves and eagles that hunt them.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Common grass of alpine pastures. Poa is among the grass genera that make up the bulk of the ibex diet, and GloBI records the snow vole eating it.
Wild goat of steep ground that eats mostly grasses, with herbs in summer and shrubs and conifer shoots in winter. The park protected the last animals; numbers rose from about 100 to about 4,000.
Mountain antelope that grazes alpine meadows in summer and moves down to forest in winter. Wolves and lynx are its historic predators.
Colonial burrowing rodent that eats grasses and herbs, fattening up for hibernation of up to nine months. It whistles an alarm when predators appear.
Small deer of the lower forests and clearings that browses leaves, shoots and herbs. GloBI records it eating bicoloured sedge.
Hare of high open ground that feeds on grasses and herbs. Recorded in the area and a main prey item of golden eagles generally.
Rock-dwelling vole of high screes and boulder fields. GloBI records it eating alpine meadow-grass.

nodes.name: Apollo
nodes.desc: Large butterfly of flower-rich mountain meadows. The caterpillars eat stonecrops and houseleeks, and the adults taste bitter to predators.
Omnivore of lower slopes. GloBI records it eating voles, shrews, frogs and lizards.
Generalist hunter and scavenger. GloBI records it eating marmots, hares, voles, roe deer and ibex.

nodes.name: Grey wolf
nodes.desc: Returned to the park area from central Italy. GloBI records it eating chamois, ibex, roe deer, marmots and foxes.
Nests near the treeline and hunts the pastures above. Marmots and hares are main prey, and it can take young ibex.
Summer sun drives a short, intense growing season on the alpine slopes.
Winter snow insulates plants and its melt feeds the pastures; deep snow also limits winter food for grazers.
The park holds 57 glaciers, and their melt waters damp meadows and streams through the summer.
Fungi, bacteria and soil invertebrates that break down dead plants and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.
